What this test does

cre-t-266 replaces the previous WIN253/cre-t-253 sub-total line (now shipped/permanent) with a new .cre-t-266-subtotal-line, injected immediately before the Add to Cart button. Control keeps the old copy ("Your sub-total is $X"), V1 reads "You're adding $X to your cart · Saving $Y", and V2 reads "N item(s) selected · $X total · Saving $Y" — V2 also syncs the Add-to-Cart button label to "ADD N ITEMS TO CART" when N>1 (confirmed live, not shown in Figma). Total = mattress price + Mattress Setup/Removal price + checked accessory add-ons.

* Safari Desktop's TC-01 8-second poll timed out for control/v1/v2 in both the original run and this final re-run — the only failure that survived all fixes. Its TC-02/03/04/05 all passed once the line had rendered, proving the line does render, just slower than the 8s poll allows on this project. See the WebKit card below.

BUG-02 — Subtotal line does not update when an accessory is added (RESOLVED — was a test artifact)

Manually re-verified live (real click, Platform Frame, V1 arm): the line updates correctly — "You're adding $2,298 to your cart · Saving $771" and the button synced to "ADD 2 ITEMS TO CART" (2,298 = 1,799 mattress + 499 Platform Frame, exactly the expected total). This pointed at a scripted-click-vs-real-click discrepancy rather than a production defect.

Fixed and fully re-verified same day — two issues in the spec:

  • clickAccessoryByName() used a JS-evaluated cb.click() (isTrusted:false) which the site's delegated listener doesn't react to the same way as a real pointer click. Switched to a real Playwright locator.click({ force: true }) (force to route around the same popup-occlusion issue the old raw-DOM-click approach existed for).
  • The post-click wait (a near-no-op regex matching any $ figure) passed instantly on the stale pre-click read, racing ahead of the site's own 500ms-interval re-render (lasting up to 3s) on fast browsers. Replaced with a direct poll on the parsed total (5s timeout) so the assertion actually waits out the site's own refresh window.
Full re-run after both fixes, all 7 browser projects, both arms: TC-04 passed 14/14 (100%) — Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari Desktop, Mobile Chrome, Mobile Safari, and Tablet iPad all correctly show the subtotal line updating to $2,298 after checking Platform Frame. BUG-02 is closed as a test-only false positive — the live subtotal-line update logic works correctly in production across every tested browser.
Bonus finding: V1 (vB.js) also shows the Add-to-Cart button syncing to "ADD 2 ITEMS TO CART" after adding an accessory — but vB.js contains no code that touches button text at all (confirmed via source read; only v2.js explicitly sets btn.textContent). This means the button-count sync is native WinkBeds site behavior present in all arms, not V2-exclusive test logic as originally assumed from the fake-click run.
Original (superseded) failure writeup, kept for history
Before the fix, this reproduced 100% in every browser project that reached the assertion cleanly (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari Desktop, Mobile Chrome, Tablet iPad, both arms, 12/12 arm-runs) with the checkbox and the page's own live accessory total updating immediately, but the rendered subtotal line text staying frozen at the pre-click amount indefinitely (expected $2,298, received $1,799). At the time this looked like a genuine functional regression rather than a timing flake, since it failed identically and deterministically across 6 browser engines. That read turned out to be wrong: it was the test's own scripted click + a too-weak wait condition, both fixed above and disproven by the 14/14 clean re-run.

BUG-01 — intermittent stale "Saving $0" (confirmed live during recon; sampled clean this run)

Per the spec's recon notes (12+ manual live trials): strikeTotal() reads a coexisting test's "Was $X" badge which populates asynchronously after the line's first render; if the badge lands outside the two short polling windows fired once from init(), the stale "Saving $0" is never corrected. This run's bounded sample (5 fresh loads × 2 arms, Chrome Desktop only) showed 0/10 mismatches — clean this time, but a clean sample doesn't retire a race condition. Treat as still open per the original recon; re-sample periodically.

Confirmed non-blocking observation — old .cro-subtotal-line selector no longer exists

Reconfirmed clean in this full run: WIN253's standalone .cro-subtotal-line element no longer exists in the DOM at all — the legacy "Your sub-total is $X" copy for control now renders through the same .cre-t-266-subtotal-line element used by V1/V2. The spec's TC-01 was corrected for this and passed cleanly in every browser except the WebKit trio below (an environment-timing issue, not a selector issue).

WebKit-engine timing/instability (Safari Desktop, Mobile Safari, Tablet iPad)

Update, second re-run: re-tested Mobile Safari and Tablet iPad in a clean environment (after clearing orphaned browser processes left over from an earlier killed run that had put the machine under memory pressure) and both came back 100% clean across all TC-01 through TC-05, both arms — no timeouts at all. This suggests at least some of the original WebKit timing failures documented below may have been caused or worsened by system resource contention during that test session, not a pure site/WebKit rendering issue. Safari Desktop's TC-01 8-second poll timeout for control/v1/v2 did reproduce again in this same re-run even before the machine hit memory pressure, so that specific failure still looks like a genuine, repeatable Safari Desktop-specific delay — the rest of the findings below should be treated as unconfirmed/environment-dependent pending another clean re-sample.

Original findings (from the first, resource-constrained run):

  • TC-01's 8-second poll timed out on Safari Desktop (2/3 arms), Mobile Safari (3/3 arms), and Tablet iPad (3/3 arms) — the injected line hadn't appeared within the window, despite the same code and settle wait that is reliable on every Chromium/Firefox run.
  • Mobile Safari additionally hit a hard navigation failure: page.goto timed out at 45000ms mid-run, breaking that arm's shared beforeAll context for the rest of the describe block (cascading "line not found" failures, then 2 tests that never ran at all). Matches the previously documented "429 wall" pattern from WIN257.
  • Not total breakage: Tablet iPad's V1 TC-03 and V2 TC-02/TC-03 passed once the line had rendered, and Mobile Safari's V2 TC-05 (console-error check) passed — reads as genuinely slower/less consistent async-injection timing under WebKit, not a broken feature.
Recommendation: consider a longer, WebKit-project-gated poll window for future WinkBeds specs rather than raising the timeout universally, since Chromium/Firefox are consistently fast.
